subtopics.title: What a Percentage Really Is — and the Decimal Trick

The single multiplier for a 15% INCREASE is:
Why is the multiplier method preferred over 'find the percentage, then add or subtract'?
options: It is the only method markers accept

subtopics.title: The Discount Step, Then the VAT Step

questions.question: After the 15% discount, the jacket's price is:
The VAT step must be applied to:
options: The discounted price of R722,50 — each step works on the previous result

questions.question: The final price of the jacket, after discount then VAT, is:
Why do the −15% and +15% NOT cancel out?
options: The VAT acted on the smaller discounted price, so it added back less than the discount removed
Because VAT is calculated differently by SARS
They do cancel — the final price is R850
Because the discount was applied second

subtopics.title: The Single Percentage Change — One Multiplier for the Whole Journey

questions.question: The combined multiplier for the whole journey (×0,85 then ×1,15) is:
A combined multiplier of 0,9775 means the overall change is:
In the percentage change formula, the denominator is always:
options: The original value — the reference point where you started
The larger of the two values

subtopics.title: Reverse Percentages — and the Full Toolkit

questions.question: A price of R830,88 INCLUDES 15% VAT. The price before VAT is found by:
Why is 'subtract 15%' (×0,85) WRONG for removing VAT from a VAT-inclusive price?
options: The VAT was calculated on the before-VAT price, so 15% of the final price is the wrong amount to remove
It is correct — both methods agree

questions.question: To undo any percentage multiplier, you:
options: Multiply by the same multiplier again

questions.question: R830,88 ÷ 1,15 returns approximately R722,50. What does this confirm?
options: The reverse calculation recovers the discounted pre-VAT price — the whole chain is consistent

questions.question: A shop takes 15% off a price. What percentage of the price is still on the plate?
R850 × 0,85 = R722,50. What does the 0,85 stand for?
options: The 85% that is left after 15% comes off

subtopics.title: Two Fifteens That Refuse to Cancel

questions.question: 15% of R850 is R127,50. How much is 15% of R722,50?
Why does the jacket end at R830,88 instead of back at R850?
options: The shop rounded the cents down
VAT in South Africa is only 14%
The VAT was worked out on the smaller R722,50, so it added back R19,13 less than the discount removed

questions.question: 0,85 × 1,15 = 0,9775. In plain words, the final price is:
The jacket dropped R19,13 in total. To turn that into a percentage you divide it by:
options: R850, the price you started at

questions.question: A till slip reads R830,88 including 15% VAT. To find the price before VAT you:
Taking 15% off R830,88 gives R706,25. Why is that the wrong pre-VAT price?
options: It removes 15% of the bigger final price, which is more VAT than was ever charged on the smaller one

questions.question: The VAT got onto the price by multiplying. It comes off again by:
options: Multiplying by the same number again

questions.question: R722,50 + R108,38 = R830,88. What are those two amounts?
options: The price before VAT and the VAT charged on it
The original price and the discount
The final price and the change owed
